story.value: Tantalum is named after Tantalus, a character from Greek mythology.
Tantalum was discovered in 1802 by Anders-Gustav Ekeberg, a Swedish chemist and mineralogist.

uses.value: Tantalum is used to make surgical sutures and implants, such as artificial joints and cranial plates.
Tantalum does not react with bodily fluids and is used to make surgical equipment.
Tantalum pentoxide, one of tantalum's compounds, is used to make capacitors.
Tantalum oxide is used to make special glass for camera lenses.
